comment: I get the appeal, though I feel like any topic with AI has to be approached with a considerable degree of caution. I personally am very against the use of AI, mostly ethically right now, because the way that it has been built and the way that it is incorporated into communities (especially the data centers being made by a lot of low-income, minority communities) is very antisocial at its core. What I am more concerned about when it comes to Buckets is, as you have mentioned, the ability for it to lie to your face. An AI cannot have trust the way a human has trust. Right now, Buckets is a app I favor because, at least for me, I trust that *you* as a human have personally exerted your time and effort to make sure that it is polished and works well. An AI can assure me or you of that, but I cannot trust it because it is simply going to regurgitate what is most probable to be said to achieve its 'prompt' or whatever else it may be tuned to optimize for. Incorporating code from an AI directly into the source code is not something I or anyone could really verify, I suppose, given it's closed-source, but it would be rough to hear it happen. What happens to a closed-source budgeting app once it's made with AI? What makes it any more appealing than an app that someone else could make with AI on a whim as well? That's the concerns I would have regarding this approach.
name: Romayne
